summary: INT. CROWNLIGHT ATRIUM – BASTION SPIRE – CORE – DAY. Sunlight pours through stained-glass crowns, casting the floor in blue, gold, red, silver.
settingText: INT. CROWNLIGHT ATRIUM – BASTION SPIRE – CORE – DAY

dialogueInline.speaker: Selene
dialogueInline.text: Sathi An. Ilion Karr. Hold Three.

directionInline: The atrium is already in the middle of a memorial, not a speech about memory. Selene reads three names from the lectern as families and officers stand under the stained-glass crowns. After the last name, she closes the register and says only that it is recorded. The doors open behind the crowd and Dominion, Keating, Kerr and Rhyne pass toward the council chamber. Venn steps aside to let a family leave before following them.
panelPlan: Tall establishing panel: Crownlight Atrium is already occupied by mourning families and uniformed officers beneath blue, gold, red and silver crown glass; the memorial is an event in progress, not ceremonial decoration.
Selene at the lectern reads the three names from an open register while stamped remembrance markers and listening faces make each loss physical.
Close on Selene closing the register after 'Recorded'; no applause, only the weight of the shut cover.
The rear doors open and Dominion, Keating, Kerr and Rhyne pass toward the council chamber through the memorial crowd rather than entering as heroes.
Venn steps aside for a grieving family leaving the atrium, then follows the Admirals at a distance, carrying the human cost into the political scene.

summary: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – CORE – DAY. A circular chamber of glass and steel.
settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – CORE – DAY

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Tal Corvus is feeding the raids. Close the approaches.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: Then say that before you call it 'all.'

directionInline: The council opens on a live map, not formal remarks. Dominion collapses the Tal Corvus approach routes on the table. Keating closes the remaining lines. Kerr points at the clinic and civilian-traffic overlays that disappear with them. The disagreement is about the actual map they are changing.
panelPlan: Establish the circular glass-and-steel council around a live Tal Corvus route map; the discussion begins with infrastructure already on the table.
Dominion collapses the primary approach routes with one controlled gesture, removing bright traffic lines from the model.
Keating closes the remaining lines until Tal Corvus is surrounded by a clean blockade ring.
Kerr activates clinic and civilian-traffic overlays; their icons disappear behind the new closure geometry as she asks about the clinics.
Hold the three Admirals across the altered map while Keating narrows her answer to inspected windows and Kerr forces the distinction between 'all' and a survivable blockade.

summary: Venn puts the success of the first green lane on the table and stakes her command credibility on making the model repeatable.
settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – CORE – DAY

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhyne
dialogueInline.text: Halev wants Verge pilots on every civilian window.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Give them the channel and the clocks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: After one crossing we almost ruined by not listening to them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: And if the second one fails?

directionInline: Rhyne puts Halev's written terms beside the replay of the first successful green crossing. Keating freezes the replay at the anomaly moment and challenges the scale of the experiment. Venn rewinds to Naomi's manual correction and makes the command commitment there. Aides continue feeding casualty and supply numbers into the table while they argue.
panelPlan: Rhyne places Halev's written terms beside replay footage of the first green crossing, pairing the political demand with evidence from the Verge.
The replay shows Naomi's manual correction during the anomaly flicker as Venn asks for Verge access to channel and clocks.
Keating freezes the image at its most dangerous instant and challenges scaling one successful crossing into policy.
Aides continue adding casualty, heater and medicine numbers around the argument; the council cannot abstract the consequences away.
Venn rewinds to Naomi's correction, accepts personal command responsibility with 'It's mine,' and leaves her name visually adjacent to the lane plan.

summary: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – CORE – DAY. A beat — charged.
settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – CORE – DAY

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: You are asking me to build a blockade around exceptions.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I'm asking you not to close the road on the people we're claiming to protect.

directionInline: Dominion leaves the blockade geometry up between himself and Venn. She does not move toward the dais or turn the answer into a declaration. The civilian route is the only gap left in the projected wall.
panelPlan: The blockade geometry remains suspended between Dominion and Venn like a literal wall, with one narrow civilian route still open.
Dominion frames the exceptions as structural weakness without leaving the dais.
Venn stays at floor level among working officers rather than advancing toward him or adopting a speech pose.
On her answer, frame Venn through the lone green gap so the road she is defending remains visible.
End on the projected civilian route inside the blockade, not either speaker, making the policy's human consequence the scene's final image.

summary: EXT. AURIC BAZAAR – GOVERNOR’S BALCONY – VERGE – SAME. A cracked monitor shows the Council live.
settingText: EXT. AURIC BAZAAR – GOVERNOR’S BALCONY – VERGE – SAME

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Two feeder routes are gone. Antibiotics are at four days.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then we don't have time for a perfect deal.

directionInline: Halev, Wallace and Naomi watch the council feed on a cracked balcony monitor while dock crews below them inventory what is actually left. Halev reads the antibiotic number from one slate; Wallace corrects him with the heat-cell count from another. Naomi watches a cargo cart leave half empty and cuts through the argument.
panelPlan: Wide from the Auric Bazaar governor's balcony: Halev, Wallace and Naomi watch the cracked council feed above dock crews counting depleted stores below.
Halev reads the four-day antibiotic figure from a battered slate while half-empty medical crates move through the background.
Wallace corrects him with the three-day heat-cell count as workers load the last usable cells onto a cargo cart.
Naomi watches that cart depart half empty, grounding her impatience in something she can physically see.
The three turn from the remote council feed toward the live docks when Naomi rejects waiting for a perfect deal.

summary: Halev makes Verge participation the price of accepting a Core blockade.
settingText: EXT. AURIC BAZAAR – GOVERNOR’S BALCONY – VERGE – SAME

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: They want our escorts inside the blockade? Fine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then a Verge pilot is on every civilian channel, and nobody closes a window without telling us first.

directionInline: Halev dictates the conditions while Naomi keys them into the live reply to the council. He is looking down at the dock queues, not up at the camera. Naomi pauses before sending because she knows how the Core will hear the demand. Halev reaches over and sends it himself.
panelPlan: Continuous on the balcony: Naomi opens a live reply channel while Halev looks down at the supply queues rather than rehearsing for camera.
Halev dictates Verge pilots on every civilian channel; Naomi enters the condition beside the blockade map.
He adds mandatory notification before any window closes as a dock alarm marks another delayed load below.
Naomi pauses over SEND and warns that the Core will resist the demand.
Halev reaches across, sends the terms himself, and answers while the waiting families remain visible past his hand.

summary: INT. VEIL MARKET – JEX’S OFFICE – SHARDS – SAME. JEX signs slates, bleeding through a fresh bandage.
settingText: INT. VEIL MARKET – JEX’S OFFICE – SHARDS – SAME

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: Blockade rumor's everywhere. Heater coils are already up twelve percent.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Because I have to sleep somewhere.

directionInline: Jex is signing contracts while a fresh bandage stains through his shirt. His scribe reads live market spikes from a slate. Jex makes one profitable decision and one deliberately less profitable one without explaining himself until the scribe asks. He keeps signing while he answers.
panelPlan: Establish Jex at a crowded worktable signing route slates in his weathered pocketed travel cloak; anomaly-glass beads bend nearby light subtly, and the fresh rib bandage is visible where the layers pull apart.
His scribe reads the twelve-percent heater-coil spike from a live market board while Jex keeps one hand moving through contracts.
Jex marks the coils for immediate sale, a clean profitable choice made without performance.
The scribe offers the blanket contract; Jex redirects it to the cheap channel while a Tal Corvus cold-weather feed plays behind them.
Jex covers the flicker of conscience with 'Because I have to sleep somewhere' and signs the next slate before the scribe can answer.

summary: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – LATER. Feeds flicker with Halev’s transmission.
settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – LATER

dialogueInline.speaker: Rhyne
dialogueInline.text: He wants to know when we close the road.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: Give him the channel. If he objects, I'd rather hear it before somebody panics.

directionInline: Halev's transmission is on the main display. Keating highlights the closure condition as if it were an incursion on command authority. Rhyne changes the label from 'VETO' to 'NOTIFICATION / LOCAL PILOT CHANNEL.' Kerr approves the practical version while Dominion watches the wording shift.
panelPlan: Halev's transmission fills the council display with the Auric dock queues visible behind him.
Keating isolates the closure condition and labels it VETO in hard military typography.
Rhyne edits the label in front of the council to NOTIFICATION / LOCAL PILOT CHANNEL, preserving the operational meaning without surrendering command.
Kerr backs the practical wording while the map shows a Verge pilot connection entering the civilian route.
Dominion watches the language and command structure change on the signed draft, saying nothing as the compromise becomes harder to remove.

summary: The Admiralty authorizes a blockade only by accepting the operating constraints forced by Venn, Rhyne, and the Verge.
settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – LATER

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Civilian windows stay published. Verge escorts stay on the channel. Venn owns the lane.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Until she gives me a reason to close it.

directionInline: The vote lights resolve by a narrow margin. The final order appears on the central table with Halev's notification language and Verge participation written into it. Keating notices those clauses before Venn does. Dominion reads the operative terms, then attaches Venn's command to the lane with a touch. Venn sees her name appear on the order and says nothing.
panelPlan: Individual vote lights resolve around the council ring until a narrow authorization majority becomes visible.
The final order expands across the central table with published windows, Verge channel access and local notification written into the operating clauses.
Keating finds the concessions first and looks across the table before Venn sees her own command assignment.
Dominion reads the terms and touches Venn's name into the lane-command field without softening his posture.
Venn watches her name appear beside the green route while the blockade authorization locks around it; she accepts without a victory line.

summary: EXT. BASTION SPIRE ORBIT – CORE – DAY. Fleet massing.
settingText: EXT. BASTION SPIRE ORBIT – CORE – DAY
directionInline: Fleet ships leave Bastion berths in layers: heavy cruisers first, destroyers rotating into the outer screen, tugs and escorts threading through them. Thunderbreak clears last. Use the scale change from dock crew to whole formation to make the blockade feel consequential without narration.
panelPlan: Open at dock-worker scale: magnetic boots on Bastion Spire's hull plating as crews pull the final service umbilicals from a heavy cruiser.
The cruiser eases out of its berth while destroyers rotate into the outer screen behind it; the formation is built in visible layers, not as a generic ship cloud.
Tugs and small escorts cross between the larger hulls, emphasizing the working traffic required to move a fleet.
Pull wider as multiple berths empty and the Crown-marked formation turns away from the ordered Core anchorage.
Final wide: Thunderbreak clears last and takes its place behind the departing formation, making Ella's responsibility legible without narration.

summary: Venn and Naomi turn political compromise into a shared operating method.
settingText: INT. THUNDERBREAK – BRIDGE – DAY

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: No, that's 'hold.' You're telling me to stop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: With your hands. Not the ship.

directionInline: Naomi teaches the Verge hand signals over a live bridge link. A junior Fleet officer gets one wrong and the bridge crew has to suppress a smile. Naomi corrects the gesture by doing it slowly in frame. Venn stands behind the officer and orders another repetition. The scene should feel like an awkward practical drill, not a unity ceremony.
panelPlan: Naomi appears on Thunderbreak's live bridge link from her smaller patched Verge cockpit, demonstrating the first hold signal with deliberate clarity.
A junior Fleet officer repeats the wrong gesture; nearby crew members suppress smiles while Naomi tells him he is ordering her ship to stop.
The officer defensively holds his hands still, earning Naomi's dry correction about holding the ship rather than his hands.
Naomi slows the motion and the officer mirrors each stage while Venn observes behind him without rescuing him.
Venn orders 'Again,' and the whole bridge repeats the Verge signal together as practical training rather than a unity tableau.

summary: Venn makes the Verge method part of Fleet procedure for the mission.
settingText: INT. THUNDERBREAK – BRIDGE – DAY
directionInline: After the call ends, Venn blanks the bridge navigation overlays. The crew suddenly has only windows, stars and one another. She makes them repeat Naomi's signals from memory. The officer who made the mistake in the previous scene gets the first one right this time.
panelPlan: The link ends and Naomi's image leaves the bridge displays, but her hand-signal chart remains on one side screen.
Venn orders the navigation overlays killed; the polished bridge abruptly loses its comforting geometry.
Crew look through real windows at stars and neighboring hulls while the junior officer from the prior scene realizes the exercise is live.
Venn gives the first signal without explanation; the officer reads it from memory and responds correctly.
Exterior consequence: Thunderbreak's adjacent escort adjusts precisely on the manual command, proving the learned method can move ships.

summary: EXT. CORE ORBIT – DRILL FIELD – CONTINUOUS. High-energy set piece: escorts corkscrew through a target shelling pattern; destroyers rotate shields in synchronized arcs; tugs practice aid-pod catches under simulated fire.
settingText: EXT. CORE ORBIT – DRILL FIELD – CONTINUOUS
directionInline: A silent drill montage: escorts corkscrew through simulated fire, destroyers rotate shields, tugs catch aid pods, and bridge crews use the new hand signals when their displays deliberately go dark. The last beat is a messy manual correction that succeeds a half-second late—useful training, not flawless ballet.
panelPlan: A Verge escort corkscrews between projected shell bursts while its pilot watches both the canopy and Naomi's manual signal feed.
Fleet destroyers rotate shield arcs in sequence; one arc arrives late, forcing the next ship to compensate rather than presenting a flawless ballet.
A utility tug catches a tumbling aid pod with its cargo cradle as simulated fire flashes across the drill field.
Inside a bridge, displays deliberately go black; gloved hands repeat the Verge signs across the command pit.
An escort overshoots the safe line by half a hull length, receives a sharp correction, and burns sideways before the simulated strike lands.
End on the rescued aid pod locked into the tug's cradle: the drill succeeds, but scorch scoring and alarm light show how narrow the margin was.

summary: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – OBSERVATION DECK – SAME. DOMINION watches the ballet.
settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – OBSERVATION DECK – SAME

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: They're teaching cruiser crews dockside hand signs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: And the drill still closes on time.

directionInline: Dominion and Keating watch the drill through observation glass. On the field below, one formation visibly breaks synchronization to recover from a simulated display loss. Kerr arrives in time to hear Keating's complaint. Dominion keeps his eyes on the clock rather than defending anyone.
panelPlan: Dominion and Keating stand behind the observation glass as the drill formation turns across Core orbit below.
A cruiser group breaks synchronization when its simulated displays fail, leaving an ugly gap in the planned geometry.
The group recovers through Verge hand signals and closes the gap before the drill clock expires.
Keating objects to dockside signs as Kerr arrives, placing the institutional argument against the successful recovery outside.
Dominion checks the completed clock instead of defending either position; the formation still finishes on time.

summary: EXT. TAL CORVUS HIGH ORBIT – SHARDS – NIGHT. A battered rock-warren glows with neon fungi.
settingText: EXT. TAL CORVUS HIGH ORBIT – SHARDS – NIGHT
directionInline: On Tal Corvus, families emerge onto balconies and catwalks to look at the growing Fleet lights overhead. A mechanic shuts down an exterior lamp to save power; the blockade remains visible after the local light goes dark. No commentary.
panelPlan: Establish Tal Corvus as a battered inhabited rock-warren: pressure-sealed additions, exposed conduits and catwalk neighborhoods spread across the asteroid while cultivated neon fungi mark breathable routes.
Families step onto narrow balconies and maintenance walks, their faces turned toward the new points of Fleet light in high orbit.
A mechanic checks a nearly depleted power meter beside an exterior work lamp.
The mechanic shuts the lamp down; local metalwork and faces fall into fungal blue-green while the blockade lights remain visible overhead.
Final long view from behind the residents: Tal Corvus is darkened by scarcity, encircled by the much brighter machinery of the Core.

summary: INT. TAL CORVUS – WARRANT HALL – NIGHT. Masked TRIARCH ENVOY whispers to captains.
settingText: INT. TAL CORVUS – WARRANT HALL – NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Emissary
dialogueInline.text: The windows are public. Test them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Then choose one that isn't full of kids.

directionInline: The emissary points out published humanitarian windows on a stolen display while captains crowd the Warren Hall. Tess sees a heater convoy listed in the next slot and steps between that line on the map and the captain reaching for it. The emissary does not threaten her; he simply moves to another target and lets the room register the refusal.
panelPlan: Establish the crowded Warrant Hall as an improvised command space: patched pressure walls, public route boards and captains beneath masked Triarch authority.
The emissary highlights published humanitarian windows on stolen Fleet telemetry and invites the captains to test them.
A captain reaches toward a listed heater convoy whose civilian cargo manifest is plainly visible.
Tess steps between the captain's hand and that route on the map, refusing the target without drawing a weapon.
The emissary shifts to another window and lets the room register Tess's refusal; the heater route remains untouched behind her.

summary: EXT. AURIC DOCKS – VERGE – DUSK. Families queue at supply halls: medkits, heat-cells, light strips.
settingText: EXT. AURIC DOCKS – VERGE – DUSK

dialogueInline.speaker: Luminara Boy
dialogueInline.text: If the wall stops their ships, how does our heater get through?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: That's what the green lights are for.

directionInline: Families queue at the Auric supply halls under a monitor showing the blockade diagram. The boy traces the solid blockade ring with a finger, then the thin green gap. His mother answers while moving their empty heat-cell carrier forward in line. The final question hangs while the monitor changes to a delayed convoy notice.
panelPlan: Auric families advance through a supply-hall queue carrying empty heat-cell frames, medkit cases and light-strip housings.
A monitor above them shows the solid blockade circle around Tal Corvus and the hair-thin green civilian gap.
The Luminara Boy traces the wall and asks how their heater passes while his mother moves their empty carrier forward.
She points to the green lights as workers behind the counter count dwindling replacement cells.
The monitor changes to CONVOY DELAYED as the boy asks whether the armed ships understand the lane.

summary: EXT. TAL CORVUS APPROACHES – SPACE – NIGHT. The blockade takes shape.
settingText: EXT. TAL CORVUS APPROACHES – SPACE – NIGHT
directionInline: The blockade locks into place around Tal Corvus. Fleet destroyers hold the outer ring; Thunderbreak anchors the published green lane; Verge escorts settle inside it. Show the humanitarian gap as physically narrow and exposed rather than reassuring.
panelPlan: Fleet destroyers settle into the outer ring around Tal Corvus, their spacing precise against the irregular rock-warren below.
Thunderbreak turns broadside at the published green-lane mouth, its position making it both shield and gatekeeper.
Verge escorts take the inner stations using tighter, locally familiar spacing than the Fleet formation.
Navigation geometry paints the humanitarian gap between armed hulls: open, clearly marked and physically narrow.
End down the length of the lane toward Tal Corvus, with every civilian ship forced to pass through an exposed corridor of waiting weapons.

summary: INT. THUNDERBREAK – BRIDGE – NIGHT. Alarms soft, steady.
settingText: INT. THUNDERBREAK – BRIDGE – NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Unknown skiff, outer ring. No weapons lock.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then let it learn we're not twitchy.

directionInline: A single Shard skiff noses toward the blockade line while Venn's bridge tracks it. Tactical's hand is already near the targeting control. Venn keeps the ship's weapons cold and watches the skiff instead of the threat board.
panelPlan: Thunderbreak's bridge tracks a lone Shard skiff approaching the outer ring; the alarm is low and steady rather than battle panic.
Tactical reports no weapons lock while their hand hovers beside the targeting control.
Venn watches the real skiff through the forward display instead of staring at the threat board.
The skiff edges closer and Tactical calls it a probe; Fleet firing geometry follows but weapons remain cold.
Venn orders restraint and Tactical deliberately moves their hand away from the control.

summary: INT. TAL CORVUS – STREET ALCOVE – NIGHT. Civilians huddle around a sputtering heater.
settingText: INT. TAL CORVUS – STREET ALCOVE – NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: SYSTEM
dialogueInline.text: Civilian window opens at 03:20. Medical, heating and food cargo only.

directionInline: Inside a cold Tal Corvus alcove, two adults and a child share a sputtering heater while the Fleet announcement crackles from an old wall speaker. One adult checks the curfew notice; the other checks the heater's failing charge. Their argument stays small because the blockade is already doing the larger talking.
panelPlan: In a cramped Tal Corvus street alcove, two adults and a child crowd around a sputtering heater with an almost-empty charge indicator.
An old wall speaker crackles with the 03:20 civilian window while patched pipes sweat cold condensation overhead.
One adult compares the time to a posted curfew notice and sees that the rules conflict.
The other checks the failing heater charge as its glow visibly weakens across the child's face.
They choose the after-curfew window without declaring it; one lifts the empty heat-cell carrier as the schedule repeats.

summary: EXT. BLOCKADE LINE – CONTINUOUS. A Confed skiff noses the line — then peels away.
settingText: EXT. BLOCKADE LINE – CONTINUOUS
directionInline: The probing Shard skiff crosses just far enough to trigger warning geometry, then peels away when nothing fires. On the Fleet side, targeting reticles track it but never turn red. Let the empty space between ships carry the tension.
panelPlan: A small Shard skiff noses across the warning boundary, dwarfed by the blockade ships holding position around it.
Fleet tracking geometry acquires the skiff; firing solutions follow its movement but remain amber rather than turning red.
Inside the skiff, the pilot holds the line for one dangerous beat, watching for the first weapon flare.
No one fires. The skiff rolls hard and peels away along the boundary.
Hold on the empty space it leaves between the two formations, with guns still trained and restraint carrying the tension.

summary: INT. VERGE ESCORT – NAOMI’S COCKPIT – SAME. Naomi’s fingers hover over the throttle.
settingText: INT. VERGE ESCORT – NAOMI’S COCKPIT – SAME
directionInline: Naomi's fingers tense on the throttle as the Shard skiff peels away. Her wingman begins to drift after it; Naomi flashes the hand sign for hold and says the line over comms. On Thunderbreak, Venn sees the correction and answers without taking control away from her.
panelPlan: Inside Naomi's patched escort cockpit, her fingers tighten over the throttle as the probing skiff rolls away.
A wingman appears off her canopy and begins drifting after the retreating target.
Naomi releases the throttle to flash the learned hold signal, reinforcing the spoken order not to pursue.
The wingman arrests the pursuit and returns to assigned spacing instead of turning the probe into a chase.
On Thunderbreak's link, Venn answers only 'Copy,' leaving the operational decision visibly with Naomi.

summary: EXT. TRAINING LANE – OUTER ARC – SAME. A DRILL CONVOY of empty tugs runs a practice through the humanitarian lane.
settingText: EXT. TRAINING LANE – OUTER ARC – SAME
directionInline: Empty tugs run the humanitarian lane under live guns. One tug deliberately loses its display and recovers on Naomi's hand signs; another overshoots a marker and is waved back by a Verge escort. Observers on both sides watch. It should look like crews learning a dangerous routine, not propaganda.
panelPlan: Two empty utility tugs enter the live humanitarian lane beneath the fixed guns of both the Fleet ring and Tal Corvus defenses.
The lead tug's display blanks on cue; its pilot looks away from the dead screen to Naomi's hand-signal relay.
A Verge escort repeats the signal through the canopy and the tug corrects by sight.
The second tug overshoots a marker; a Verge pilot waves it back while a Fleet targeting crew visibly holds fire.
Observers on both sides watch the ungainly correction instead of applauding it.
End with both tugs clearing the far marker: an ordinary-looking crossing made difficult enough to show why the routine matters.

summary: INT. VEIL MARKET – JEX’S OFFICE – NIGHT. Jex watches six feeds at once: blockades, docks, street-level queues.
settingText: INT. VEIL MARKET – JEX’S OFFICE – NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Put the heaters on the permit.

directionInline: Jex watches six feeds while his scribe holds two contracts for the same shipment. One legal route pays badly; one black-market route pays well. He looks at a feed of families waiting for heater cells before choosing the permit for that cargo, then immediately pulls the next, less sympathetic contract toward himself.
panelPlan: Jex works before six feeds: blockade geometry, Auric docks, cold street queues, permit clocks, market prices and Shard traffic.
His scribe holds two contracts for the same heater shipment—legal permit at three and off-books delivery at nine.
Jex studies families waiting with empty heat-cell carriers, his fresh rib bandage tightening as he shifts in the pocketed cloak.
He stamps the heater cargo onto the low-paying permit route and hands it back before conscience becomes performance.
Jex pulls a less essential, more profitable contract toward himself and denies sudden respectability while the heater permit enters the queue.

summary: The first real Tal Corvus convoy tests the compromise; discipline, not rhetoric, gets civilians through an anomaly flicker.
settingText: EXT. BLOCKADE LINE – HOURS LATER
directionInline: The first loaded Tal Corvus convoy enters with heater cores, medpods and batteries visible. A glassy duplicate destroyer appears directly across the Fleet firing solution. Naomi shuts off her display and gives the manual signs from the previous drill; Verge escorts respond, then Fleet crews copy them. One escort waits on her hand instead of firing at the ghost. The real convoy passes the anomaly and physically reaches the receiving dock before anyone celebrates.
panelPlan: Loaded convoy enters the narrow green lane; cargo is visibly medical/heating supplies.
A glassy duplicate destroyer appears across a Fleet firing solution; targeting boards disagree with what crews see.
Naomi kills her display and signals by hand. One Verge escort follows; a Fleet bridge officer recognizes the same sign.
Ships move on deliberately different manual cues while the ghost stays in place. Nobody fires.
Receiving dock: the first heater core is physically rolled off the freighter. Only then does the crowd react.

summary: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – NIGHT. Reports scroll.
settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: Zero incidents doesn't make it safe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: No. It makes it zero incidents.

directionInline: The council reads the actual after-action numbers: zero shots, medicine delivered, heaters installed. Keating circles the anomaly report rather than the success count. Kerr answers without overselling the result. Dominion advances the schedule to the next window.
panelPlan: After-action figures scroll around the council table: zero shots fired, medicine delivered and heater units installed.
Kerr follows the cargo counts while Keating enlarges the anomaly incident instead.
Keating warns that zero incidents does not establish safety; the ghost-destroyer image hangs above the table.
Kerr answers precisely, refusing both panic and triumph.
Dominion advances the schedule to the next civilian window and keeps it open, turning measured result into continued policy.

summary: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – NIGHT. He signs an order: BLOCKADE: ACTIVE.
settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON – ADMIRALTY COUNCIL – NIGHT
directionInline: Dominion signs the blockade order. Beneath BLOCKADE: ACTIVE, the smaller clauses remain visible: published humanitarian windows, Verge integration, local notification. His stylus pauses over the concessions for one beat, then signs across all of it.
panelPlan: Dominion sits alone at the head of the council table while operational reports continue scrolling across the surrounding glass.
Close on the order title, BLOCKADE: ACTIVE, above the smaller binding clauses for published humanitarian windows, Verge integration and local notification.
His stylus stops over the concessions; reflected in the glass, the council chamber's crown geometry divides his face without changing his expression.
Dominion signs across the full order, including the clauses he opposed.
The authorization propagates from the council slate to the Tal Corvus tactical display, turning political language into an active ring of ships.

summary: Venn watches the lane become routine and understands that routine is the victory she has to defend.
settingText: EXT. THUNDERBREAK – HULL WALK – NIGHT
directionInline: On the maintenance gantry, Venn watches tugs unload while crews reset beacon clocks for the next window. She checks the manifest herself and asks the only question that matters to her now. The officer's answer is boring; Venn is visibly satisfied by that. She hands the slate back and goes inside.
panelPlan: Venn walks Thunderbreak's maintenance gantry while ordinary tugs unload heater cells and medpods through the green window below.
Crews reset physical beacon clocks for the next crossing; the work resembles a shift change rather than a battle operation.
Venn takes the manifest slate herself and checks arrivals against cargo moving off the tugs.
She asks for the late list; the officer's empty answer is boring enough to become the victory.
Venn returns the slate after her restrained approval and heads inside as the crews continue without ceremony.

summary: Billie decides the new lane must be broken before it becomes normal; Tess decides civilians will not be the proof.
settingText: EXT. BLACK DRIFT HAVEN – SHARDS – NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: They're already calling it the regular window.

directionInline: Billie has stolen the published schedule and is marking targets on it with grease pencil. Tess does not argue in abstractions; she sees Billie's circle land on the third slot and recognizes the evacuation manifest attached to it. Billie knows exactly what she has marked. Tess leaves before Billie finishes enjoying the reaction.
panelPlan: At Black Drift Haven, Billie spreads the stolen schedule across a scarred gantry table and marks targets with grease pencil.
Tess arrives as Billie complains that crews already call it the regular window; neither closes the distance between them.
Billie circles tomorrow's third slot with deliberate pleasure rather than random aggression.
Tess turns the schedule enough to expose the evacuation manifest and makes Billie acknowledge who occupies that slot.
Billie answers 'I know'; Tess leaves toward Gravefire before Billie can enjoy the reaction, carrying action into the tag.

summary: Tess commits Gravefire to the threatened evacuation window.
settingText: EXT. BLACK DRIFT HAVEN – SHARDS – NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire to Tal Corvus. Put the evac run on my transponder.

directionInline: Tess is already in Gravefire's cockpit when Billie looks up from the schedule. She keys her transponder onto the threatened third slot and launches. End on the route display: Billie's target mark and Gravefire's identifier now occupy the same window.
panelPlan: Continuous from Billie's marked schedule: Tess has already crossed the gantry and reached Gravefire's cockpit before Billie looks up.
Tess straps in as the threatened third-slot evacuation manifest glows beside Billie's grease-pencil target mark on the copied schedule.
She keys Gravefire's transponder into that same window and delivers the call without a speech.
Gravefire releases from Black Drift Haven and burns toward Tal Corvus while the haven's welded wreckage falls behind it.
Final inset on the route display: Billie's target mark and GRAVEFIRE occupy the same evacuation window, converting their argument into an unavoidable next action.
